svg.text: TERMINATION DRAWING — RAIL X3 (24 V DC DIGITAL)
P-101 equipment block, terminals X3:001–030 · field side left, internal side right · 20 % spare terminals grouped at the end of the block
LCS-101 Start PB — 24 V DC out
LCS-101 Stop PB — 24 V DC out
Seal water flow switch — 24 V DC out
SCREEN EARTH BAR XS (rail X3 block)
earth bar. FAT test E-35 verifies
SCREEN EARTHING — PUT THIS ON THE DRAWING, NOT ONLY IN THE SPEC
SCREEN EARTHED AT MCC END ONLY — DO NOT EARTH AT FIELD END
The installer reads the termination drawing. They will probably never read the
specification. One line of text on the drawing face prevents an entire class of
commissioning fault — noisy, drifting analogue readings from earth loops.
Sequential from 001. No gaps, no re-use. Grouped by
equipment in the same order as the schematic sheets.
A deleted circuit's terminal becomes a SPARE and keeps its
number. Re-using a number means an old drawing and a new
drawing disagree, and someone will eventually work from the
20 % minimum, contiguous at the end of each equipment block.
Distributed spares look tidy and are nearly useless —
you can never fit a new multicore's cores together.
SHEET-PATH, e.g. 0101-14 = sheet SCH-0101, current path 14.
Ferruled both ends. Any wire in the board tells you which
Fitted between voltage groups. Routinely forgotten —
it is part of the segregation design, not decoration.
1. SCREEN EARTHED AT MCC END ONLY. Do NOT earth instrument or control screens at the field end. This note is repeated on the drawing face
because the installer reads the drawing, not the specification.
2. VSD motor cable screens are the EXCEPTION — they are terminated 360° at BOTH ends via EMC glands. Different problem, different solution.
3. Terminal markers are printed FROM this schedule, never hand-written. FAT defect FD-006b was two transposed markers, which would have
caused future wiring errors by someone who correctly followed the schedule.
4. C-0102 was changed from 12 core to 16 core at Rev B. The schedule used all 12 cores, leaving no spares. Four extra cores cost almost nothing;
a second cable pull through an operating plant costs a variation and an access permit.
5. Maximum two conductors per terminal, and only where the terminal is rated for it. Verified at FAT test D-33.
